what: BF16-ATTR, BF16-KERN and BF16-PANELS-1 (2026-10-18): the bf16 contract's GEMMs taken apart at the 9.84M decoder's 13 shapes, and two changes that keep every state bit for bit. BF16-KERN: the AMX kernel loads its B tiles as streamed (TILELOADDT1) and prefetches the next block's lines of C for writing during the depth loop (PREFETCHW); every tile operation is the one before, in the same order. BF16-PANELS-1: the SwiGLU block's outputs -- the hidden activation, the gate and up projections' adjoints -- are written by their producers as the bf16 GEMMs' panels (each element the binary32 value's conversion, where the pack puts it for a whole call: the hidden activation as A and as B, each adjoint as A and as A^T, the two filling the binary32 slot) and read pre-packed: bcir_tensor_silu_mul_panels_pool, bcir_tensor_swiglu_backward_panels_pool and bcir_tensor_mm_bf16_group_panels_pool (bcir_tensor.h). The trainer takes them under the bf16 contract with no provider when every GEMM they feed is whole 32-tiles (the rows, the model's width and the hidden width multiples of 32) and the slots are 64-byte aligned; otherwise binary32 and the packs, as before.

Only measurements taken within one process compare trees: kern's candidates rotated over the same packs, block's two arms alternated, steppair's three libraries a step each in turn. The two phases records of a thread count were two processes, minutes apart, so their difference is not the kernel's gain (kern's is).
